_comment: What's new cards. One key per kit version, one short line per highlight.
The installer draws a card for every version it crossed during an upgrade,
and `exakit whats-new [version]` reads the same lines. This file is the only
source: there is nothing else to keep in step.
Rules, enforced by tests/whats-new.sh so a bad line cannot reach a user:
- a line is at most 68 characters, or the card would truncate it to '...'
- at most 6 lines per version, or the card stops being skimmable
- a version key is a plain dotted number (0.2.0), because the installer
sorts them to decide which cards a jump like 0.1.0 -> 0.4.0 crosses
- lines stay ASCII. PowerShell 5.1 reads a BOM-less file through the
legacy ANSI codepage, so an em dash here renders as garbage on Windows
- the same trap tests/ps-encoding-guard.sh catches in .ps1 files but
cannot see in a data file
Write what the reader can now DO, not what changed in the code. A first
install shows no cards at all, so every line here is read by someone who
already had the kit working and wants to know what is different.
0.2.3: Security: uv, which runs the MCP server, is pinned and verified.
No installer script is downloaded and executed any more.
A uv older than 0.13.4 is never run (compromised root CA upstream).
Yours is left alone; below the floor the kit installs its own copy.
exakit status names an old uv; exakit update uv installs the pin.
exakit version shows a uv row like every other component.
0.2.2: The launcher now downloads from Exasol's own server (S3), verified.
If that server is unreachable, the verified GitHub release is used.
Pinning another launcher version still takes the GitHub release.
EXAKIT_PERSONAL_S3=0 skips that server if your network blocks it.
0.2.1: exakit start|stop <service> acts on one service, not everything.
exakit stop database asks before taking it from running add-ons.
exakit update --json answers one object with what happened.
Loading a file onto a table with rows asks: skip, replace or append.
exasol-scheduler installs straight from its own GitHub release.
Every --json output is laid out to read, with one formatter.
0.2.0: exakit update applies the recommended updates, latest AI skills.
exakit version shows installed and recommended versions.
truly agentic, every command speaks JSON with clear exit codes.
